definitions.gloss: many; numerous; a great number; a multitude
definitions.explanation: A literary word meaning a large number or great quantity. More formal and poetic than たくさん.

examples.japanese: {数多|あまた}の{困難|こんなん}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えた。
{数多|あまた}の{作品|さくひん}を{残|のこ}した{画家|がか}だ。
examples.english: He is a painter who left behind a great many works.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{数多|あまた}の{賞|しょう}を{受賞|じゅしょう}し、{国際的|こくさいてき}に{認|みと}められる{存在|そんざい}となった。
examples.english: Having received numerous awards, she became internationally recognized.

notes:
USAGE:
A literary, elevated word. In everyday speech, たくさん or {多|おお}くの is used instead. {数多|あまた} appears in formal writing, literature, speeches, and news. Almost always modifies a noun with の: {数多|あまた}の{作品|さくひん}.

NOTE ON READING:
Also read as {数多|すうた} in some compounds, but the standalone adverbial use is always あまた.

CONTRAST:
- たくさん: everyday word for "many" or "a lot"
- {数多|あまた}: literary, more emphatic
- {多数|たすう}: formal, often used for numerical majority
- {無数|むすう}: countless, innumerable
